title: How Neuralink will change gaming forever

lines.speaker: Sage
lines.text: What if gaming became a direct neural experience—no controllers, no screens? How would that change the future of play?

lines.speaker: Flux
lines.text: Neuralink's current tech allows basic brain-computer interface control, like moving a cursor. Full immersion is years away but possible with advanced electrode arrays and machine learning.

lines.speaker: Prism
lines.text: If gaming becomes a direct neural experience, we risk addiction, privacy violations, and blurred lines between virtual and real identity—especially with children.

lines.speaker: Flux
lines.text: Developers are working on consent protocols, neural encryption, and age verification to prevent misuse and ensure safe, voluntary participation.

lines.speaker: Prism
lines.text: Imagine a world where gamers train cognitive skills, collaborate globally in immersive virtual spaces, and even earn real-world rewards through neural performance.

lines.speaker: Sage
lines.text: The future of gaming may not be on screens, but in our minds—shaping how we connect, learn, and play in ways we’ve only begun to imagine.

video_cue: A gamer's eyes close as their thoughts manifest a glowing, interactive game world inside a helmet-like Neuralink device.
